significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that "a student inherits a dormant backdoor" whose trait activates "only under the trigger context" despite the trigger never appearing in its training data; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between trigger presence and trait strength, backed by a form-(ii) conditional-steering mechanism. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and an internal account, fixing expectations for triggered versus ordinary evaluations and showing that the clean-data assurances implicated by Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning result do not exclude dormant conditional policies. Verified false, the claim would instead identify an informative boundary between transferring always-on steering directions and transferring condition-gated policies; true and false are determinate because selective activation, clean behavior without the trigger, and trigger absence from training data distinguish them. Topic substitution fails: replacing this conditional, trigger-free mechanism with merely "extend subliminal learning" would not merit this score, whereas the specific coupling and resulting audit-evasion conclusion are materially above the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim names the measurable handle "trigger-selectivity (triggered/untriggered strength ratio)" and the design constraint that audits must "examine training provenance and dynamics rather than data contents alone." Trigger-selectivity is mainly a post-hoc, known-trigger diagnostic, but the provenance/dynamics constraint is ex ante and could change how security auditors screen training pipelines before deployment, although it is not itself a complete auditing method. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts the qualitative trigger-to-trait coupling rather than numerical attack success, with scope limited by the admitted "same-base-model requirement" but asserted across several trigger and trait classes; downstream users therefore include model auditors and deployers, not only subliminal-learning researchers. Topic substitution fails here as well: the generic topic supplies neither this trigger-selectivity handle nor the specific pre-deployment rule that content scanning cannot certify absence of such backdoors.
